pov: 本章为第三人称有限视角，全程贴 Helena，无视角切换。证据：L35「Helena couldn’t stop thinking about Cynthia.」开篇即 Helena 的内心；L59「But instead, emptiness echoed in her chest.」直接写她的体感；L65「Her magic had been malfunctioning since Cynthia left.」她的魔法状态；L152「Helena knew her eyes were shifting from grey to silver」以 knew 标记认知归属；L201「she reached into her core where her magic waited」她的内探。非视角人物『心声』逐条核查：①L71「raised a knowing brow and whined.」——Hamlet 的『knowing（了然）』是 Helena 的拟人化解读/叙述修辞，不是 Hamlet 的真实心声；②L101「His golden eyes pierced the secrets hiding in her soul.」——是 Helena 的被注视感受，非 Hamlet 视角；③L116「And he was trying to break it to her gently.」——紧接 L113 心声「I’m wrong.」，是 Helena 的推断，不是叙述者全知断言；④L143「There was unmistakable menace in Sinclair’s gleaming smile.」——Helena 的观察判断，Sinclair 全章无内心描写；⑤L125「Damien Sinclair’s voice fell like a stone in deep water.」——Helena 的听觉比喻。Lachlan、Ellie、Sinclair 均只有外部言行，无心声。

scene_split.when: 紧承上段的白天，Helena 上门求参与调查之后

events.did: Helena 无法停止想念 Cynthia
events.verbatim: Helena couldn’t stop thinking about Cynthia.

events.did: 她在药店加了额外的班让自己忙起来，但没有用
events.verbatim: She took on extra shifts at the apothecary to keep herself busy, but it did no good.

events.did: 每次门铃响她都心跳加速，发现来者不是 Cynthia 又心往下坠
events.verbatim: Her heart jumped every time the bell rang and plummeted each time it wasn’t Cynthia.

events.did: Helena 加入 Ellie 的送货行程，一起给年长邻居送魔法药剂、护肤膏和美味的非魔法烘焙点心
events.verbatim: She joined Ellie on her rounds as she delivered magical potions and lotions, and non-magical but delicious baked goods to some of their elderly neighbours

events.did: 这些老人是心软的表亲 Ellie 主动照拂的人
events.verbatim: people her soft-hearted cousin had taken under her wing.

events.did: 好心的老人们开始抱怨 Helena 的尖酸话语与不祥眼神
events.verbatim: But the kindly folks started to grumble about Helena’s acerbic comments and baleful glances.

events.did: 第三次投诉之后，Ellie 温和建议 Helena 去跟 Lachlan 叔谈谈在 Scotland Yard 协助他办案
events.verbatim: After the third complaint, Ellie gently suggested Helena speak with Uncle Lachlan about assisting him at Scotland Yard.

events.did: 他（Lachlan）帮不上忙
events.verbatim: He was no help.

events.did: Helena 恳求他允许她参与调查 Hubert 谋杀案的任何线索；他在杂乱的办公室里满口粗话、来回跺脚
events.verbatim: When Helena begged him to allow her to investigate any leads they had on Hubert’s murder, amongst much foul language and stomping around his cluttered office,

events.did: 他宣布了这个气人的消息：案件陷入僵局
events.verbatim: he delivered the infuriating news that the case was at a standstill.

events.did: Sinclair 对 Seven Dials 穷苦人的掌控是一股密不透风的力量
events.verbatim: Damien Sinclair’s power over the poor people of Seven Dials was an impenetrable force.

events.did: 无论警方给多少贿赂、他的警察下多少威胁、许多少赦免旧罪的承诺，没人开口作证
events.verbatim: No matter what bribes they offered, how many threats his bobbies made, or what promises they gave of forgiving past crimes, no one was talking.

events.did: 更糟的是，他将被派去 Bath，就贵族富豪中连发的盗窃案与当地警长会商
events.verbatim: he was being sent to Bath to consult with the superintendent there on a rash of robberies taking place amongst wealthy members of the peerage.

events.did: Helena 质问：这是不是意味着你们放弃找 Hubert Burrows 的凶手了
events.verbatim: ‘Does that mean you’ve given up on finding Hubert Burrows’ murderer?’

events.did: 她压不住愤慨，话语被泡得带酸带刺
events.verbatim: Helena couldn’t stop the outrage soaking her words in acid.

events.did: Lachlan 说凶手已经找到了，就是 Damien Sinclair，像『这是我脸上的鼻子』一样清楚
events.verbatim: ‘We’ve found his murderer. It’s Damien Sinclair, as clearly as this is the nose on my face.

events.did: 只是他还证明不了——暂时（Yet 独立成句）
events.verbatim: I just canna prove it. Yet.

events.did: 他要 Helena 记住他的话：Sinclair 会失手，到时候他们会做好准备
events.verbatim: But mark my words, lass. He’ll slip up. And when he does, we’ll be ready.’

events.did: Helena 指出：Lachlan 叔人在 Bath，根本谈不上准备好抓那个混蛋
events.verbatim: When Helena pointed out Uncle Lachlan could hardly be ready to catch the bastard if he was in Bath,

events.did: Lachlan 一记致命的眼神让 Helena 想起此人曾是女王军队里令人胆寒的军人
events.verbatim: Uncle Lachlan’s lethal glare reminded Helena the man had once been a deadly and fearsome soldier in her majesty’s army.

events.did: 她告辞离开，Hamlet 紧贴着她的脚后跟
events.verbatim: She took her leave with Hamlet close on her heels.

events.did: 为了转移注意力，Helena 主动认领药店里人人都讨厌的那一件活：盘点库存
events.verbatim: In desperation for distraction, Helena volunteered for the one job they all hated at the apothecary: inventory.

events.did: 她干到深夜，远在最后一位客人离店之后
events.verbatim: She worked late into the night, long after the last customer left the shop,

events.did: 逐件清点并登记：每罐除皱膏、每袋浴盐、每瓶皮肤精华、每捆净化鼠尾草
events.verbatim: counting and recording every pot of wrinkle salve, sachet of bath salts, vial of skin serum, and bushel of cleansing sage.

events.did: 回家的画面（Rowan 姨在餐桌边救治病弱的植物、Ellie 用她们的烤箱烘焙美味）本该让 Helena 满心温暖欢喜
events.verbatim: The idea of going home where Aunt Rowan would no doubt be working on healing an ailing plant at the dinner table while Ellie baked something delicious in their oven should have filled Helena with warm joy.

events.did: 但实际上她胸口只回荡着空洞
events.verbatim: But instead, emptiness echoed in her chest.

events.did: 因为她曾经充实的人生突然显得中空
events.verbatim: Because her once full life suddenly felt hollow.

events.did: 她失手摆弄那瓶用春分采收的碎番红花花瓣浸制的 witch hazel 爽肤水，骂自己手指打滑
events.verbatim: Fumbling the bottle of witch hazel tonic infused with crushed crocus petals harvested during the vernal equinox, Helena cursed her slippery fingers.

events.did: 由于玻璃上凝水，她已经打碎了三瓶抗炎药剂
events.verbatim: She had already broken three of the anti-inflammatory potions as condensation gathered on the glass.

events.did: 水洼不断在她脚边形成
events.verbatim: Puddles kept forming around her feet,

events.did: 她得先拖完地再回家，否则早上等着 Clio 的会是水渍
events.verbatim: she would need to mop the floor before heading home or there would be water stains waiting for Clio in the morning.

events.did: 自 Cynthia 离开后，她的魔法一直失灵
events.verbatim: Her magic had been malfunctioning since Cynthia left.

events.did: 平时她能屏蔽别人的念头，除非对方情绪特别强烈，或她刻意潜入其脑中找秘密
events.verbatim: Usually, she could ignore people’s thoughts unless they were especially emotional, or if she purposefully delved into their minds seeking secrets.

events.did: 可近来只要一出家门，脑中就像有持续不断的低语入侵
events.verbatim: But of late, it was like a constant murmur invading her head whenever she left the house.

events.did: 手指上积水、衣服总是潮的、眼睛闪银光的次数多过灰色
events.verbatim: Water gathered on her fingers, her clothes were always damp, and her eyes flashed silver more often than grey.

events.did: Helena 出声自语：太可笑了，我得放下她
events.verbatim: ‘This is ridiculous. I need to get over her.’

events.did: Hamlet 早已在柜台角落（收钱和放销售账本的地方）的专属软垫上安顿如家
events.verbatim: Hamlet, who had made himself at home on his special pillow in the corner next to the counter where they collected money and kept the ledger of sales,

events.did: 它挑起一副了然的眉毛，发出呜咽
events.verbatim: raised a knowing brow and whined.

events.did: Helena 说：继续牵着她（Cynthia）不公平；爱对我来说不是选项，而她值得被爱
events.verbatim: ‘Holding onto her isn’t fair. Love isn’t an option for me, and she deserves love.’

events.did: Hamlet 翻起上唇露出一排尖牙，颈毛倒竖，低吼起来
events.verbatim: Curling his upper lip to show a row of sharp teeth, Hamlet growled as his hackles rose.

events.did: 连她的使魔都不站在她这边
events.verbatim: Even her familiar wasn’t on her side.

events.did: Helena 叫它：Hamlet！
events.verbatim: ‘Hamlet!’

events.did: 它吠叫，尖利的声音划破安静的房间
events.verbatim: He barked, a piercing sound in the quiet room.

events.did: 怒气像暴涨的河水一样升起
events.verbatim: Anger rose like a swollen river.

events.did: Helena 反驳（对 Hamlet）：别数落我！我痛恨把 Cynthia 送走，痛恨我们分离的每一刻
events.verbatim: ‘Don’t scold me! I hated sending Cynthia away. I hate every moment we are apart.

events.did: 但她无法改变自己的过去，也无法改变母亲留下的遗产
events.verbatim: But I can’t help my past. Or the legacy my mother left.

events.did: 她不肯冒险变成母亲那样：被爱蒙蔽到看不见真相
events.verbatim: And I won’t risk becoming like her, Hamlet. I won’t be so blinded by love, I lose sight of the truth.’

events.did: 她母亲的爱曾是绝望之物，是吞噬一切入其深处的漩涡
events.verbatim: Her mother’s love had been a desperate thing. An all-consuming whirlpool sucking everything into its depths.

events.did: 铁匠对 Willow 的欲望扭曲、变质，并毁了她
events.verbatim: And the blacksmith’s desire for Willow had twisted, warped, and destroyed her.

events.did: 他们（母亲与铁匠）共有的爱是有毒的、有害的、毁灭性的
events.verbatim: The love they had shared was toxic. Poisonous. Devastating.

events.did: （无引号心声）可是 Cynthia 永远不会伤害我
events.verbatim: But Cynthia would never hurt me.

events.did: 这声低语像河漩上的一片叶子浮了上来
events.verbatim: The whisper surfaced like a leaf on a river’s eddy.

events.did: Hamlet 从软垫上起身，沿过道小跑，一路绕开水洼，停在她脚边，把头撞向她的膝盖
events.verbatim: Hamlet rose from his pillow and padded down the aisle, side-stepping puddles along the way. He stopped at her feet and bumped his head into her knee.

events.did: Helena 蹲坐到地板上，裙子又吸了一摊水，手里捧着那瓶 witch hazel 爽肤水
events.verbatim: Helena dropped to the floor, her dress soaking up yet another pool of water as she cradled the witch hazel tonic in her hand.

events.did: 照这速度，她会因失控的魔法浑身湿透地走回家，全店的瓶子都会挂满水珠
events.verbatim: At this rate, she would walk home soaking wet from her mismanaged magic, and all the bottles in the store would be spotted with droplets.

events.did: 她说：不是所有生物都生来适合那样的爱，Hamlet
events.verbatim: ‘Not all creatures are built for love like that, Hamlet.’

events.did: 它用后腿跃起，双爪搭上她的手臂，金色的眼睛看穿她灵魂里藏着的秘密
events.verbatim: Jumping on his hind feet, he put both paws on her arm. His golden eyes pierced the secrets hiding in her soul.

events.did: 『我没说错。』她下巴颤抖
events.verbatim: ‘I’m not wrong.’ Her chin quivered.

events.did: 它伸长脖子舔了她的脸颊——相伴以来它从不屑于做出这种犬类行为
events.verbatim: He stretched his neck and licked her cheek. In all of their days together, he had never lowered himself to such canine behaviour.

events.did: （无引号心声）哦。天哪。女神啊
events.verbatim: Oh. Dear. Goddess.

events.did: （无引号心声）我错了
events.verbatim: I’m wrong.

events.did: 她的女巫会知道、Rowan 姨知道、那只狐狸知道，而 Hamlet 在设法委婉地把这一点讲给她听
events.verbatim: Her coven knew it. Aunt Rowan knew it. The fox knew it. And he was trying to break it to her gently.

events.did: Hamlet 轻吠一声，恰在此时前门铃轻响，皮革拍在湿木头上
events.verbatim: Hamlet yipped just as the bell to the front door tinkled and leather slapped onto wet wood.

events.did: 『该死。』Helena 低声说，起身快步绕过货架走向过道——她忘了锁前门
events.verbatim: ‘Damnation,’ Helena whispered, standing and walking swiftly down the aisle around the shelf. She had forgotten to lock the front door.

events.did: 她道歉说今天打烊、明天某时再开门——话死在喉咙里（时间未说出）
events.verbatim: ‘I’m sorry. We’re closed for the day. We open again tomorrow at—’ The words died in her throat.

events.did: Hamlet 贴在她脚边，这次它胸腔里滚出的低吼带着真正的凶意
events.verbatim: Hamlet was at her heel. The growl rumbling from his chest this time held true menace.

events.did: 来人开口：Blair 小姐，正想找的就是你——是 Damien Sinclair
events.verbatim: ‘Miss Blair. Just the woman I was ’oping to find.’

events.did: Sinclair 的声音像石头坠入深水
events.verbatim: Damien Sinclair’s voice fell like a stone in deep water.

events.did: Helena 质问：你到底在这儿干什么
events.verbatim: ‘What the devil are you doing here?’

events.did: Sinclair 说他听说太多对 All Things Bright and Beautiful 的赞美，有人称它是全英格兰最好的女性美容品店
events.verbatim: ‘I’ve ’eard so many compliments about All Things Bright and Beautiful. Some say it’s the finest store for women’s beauty products in all of England.

events.did: 远胜 Madame Rachel’s；据说店里卖的药剂恢复女性青春美貌之效近乎巫术
events.verbatim: Far superior to Madame Rachel’s. Apparently, the potions you sell are so effective at restoring a woman’s youth and beauty, it’s akin to witchcraft.’

events.did: Helena 忍不住嗤之以鼻：我可不信你跟我们的顾客有来往，Sinclair
events.verbatim: Helena couldn’t stop the snort of disbelief. ‘I hardly think you converse with our clientele, Sinclair.’

events.did: 这个黑黝黝英俊的男人挑起一道午夜色的眉毛：我会往来的人物之『品质』会让你吃惊，Blair 小姐
events.verbatim: The darkly handsome man raised a midnight brow. ‘You would be surprised at the quality of company I keep, Miss Blair.’

events.did: Hamlet 的低吼愈发强烈
events.verbatim: Hamlet’s growl increased in intensity.

events.did: Sinclair 闪着光的微笑里有毫不掩饰的威胁
events.verbatim: There was unmistakable menace in Sinclair’s gleaming smile.

events.did: 『我们打烊了。马上离开。』Helena 强迫自己的声音里带上钢铁
events.verbatim: ‘We are closed. Leave now.’ Helena forced steel into her voice.

events.did: Sinclair：哦，可我来这儿是为找一种别处找不到的特定产品
events.verbatim: ‘Oh, but I’m ’ere for a certain product not to be found anywhere else.’

events.did: Helena 从空气中抽取水分，知道自己的眼睛正由灰转银——她需要武装自己
events.verbatim: Pulling moisture from the air, Helena knew her eyes were shifting from grey to silver, but she needed to arm herself.

events.did: 因为 Damien Sinclair 走出 Seven Dials 只有一个目的：挑起战争
events.verbatim: Because Damien Sinclair only came out of Seven Dials for one purpose: to start a war.

events.did: Helena 决不容许他不带几道战损就离开这家药店
events.verbatim: And Helena would be damned if she let him leave the apothecary without a few battle scars.

events.did: 泛滥的江河能片刻间放倒橡树，能托起船、淹没村庄、重塑大地
events.verbatim: Flooding rivers could fell an oak tree in moments. It could lift a ship, drown a village, and reshape the earth.

events.did: 她的巫水能轻易卷走 Sinclair 这样的魔鬼
events.verbatim: Her witchwater would easily sweep away a devil like Sinclair.

events.did: 她一掌上翻、另一掌扣在上面，魔力积聚成掌心一旋海蓝色水涡，等她以意念塑成足以切穿石头的激流
events.verbatim: Holding one hand palm up and cupping the other over it, her magic built, pooling into a swirl of aquamarine in her palm, waiting for her thoughts to form it into a spray powerful enough to cut through stone.

events.did: 她下最后通牒：这是你毫发无损离开的最后机会；无论你要找什么，这里都没有
events.verbatim: ‘This is your last chance to leave unscathed, Sinclair. Whatever you seek, you won’t find it here.’

events.did: Sinclair：我要找的是一名女巫，Blair 小姐
events.verbatim: ‘I seek a witch, Miss Blair.’

events.did: Helena 让元素之力贯穿全身
events.verbatim: Helena let the elemental force sweep through her.

events.did: Seven Dials 的魔鬼也许正在猎捕女巫，但她拒绝做任何人的猎物
events.verbatim: The Devil of Seven Dials might be hunting witches, but she refused to be anyone’s prey.

events.did: Hamlet 的咆哮陡然尖化成恐惧的呜叫，同时有重物猛击在她后脑（施动者未点名）
events.verbatim: Hamlet’s snarl abruptly sharpened into a yelp of fear as something heavy slammed into the back of her head.

events.did: 世界陷入黑暗（她昏了过去）
events.verbatim: The world went dark.

events.did: Helena 最先感觉到的是热；她像在火焰中呼吸
events.verbatim: Helena felt the heat first. She was breathing in flames.

events.did: 干燥的空气以令人窒息的一波抽走她体内的所有水分
events.verbatim: Dry air sucked any moisture from her body in a suffocating wave.

events.did: 她眨眼，盐刺痛了她的眼睛、模糊了视线
events.verbatim: She blinked as salt stung her eyes and blurred her vision.

events.did: 她试着把手臂从头顶上方的固定处拉下来，皮革绑带勒进手腕
events.verbatim: Leather ties bit into her wrists when she tried to pull her arms from where they were secured above her head.

events.did: 腕铐上连着金属链；她拼命挣，链子叮嘎作响，却在低矮天花板的大横梁固定处一寸不让
events.verbatim: Metal chains were attached to the cuffs around her wrists. They clinked and creaked as she strained against them, but didn’t give an inch where they were secured to a large beam in the low ceiling.

events.did: 有人脱掉了她的连衣裙、衬裙、束腰和裙撑；她只穿着一件内衣
events.verbatim: Someone had removed her dress, petticoats, corset, and bustle. She wore only her shift

events.did: 要不是在如此干热的环境里一想到厚重衣物就让她想抓破自己的皮，她本会对 Sinclair 扒她衣服这件事感到愤怒（虚拟语气：实际上没有愤怒）
events.verbatim: and would have been outraged at Sinclair undressing her if the very idea of heavy clothes in such a dry, hot environment didn’t make her want to claw out of her skin.

events.did: 『我到底在哪儿？』她的声音只是沙哑的气声
events.verbatim: ‘Where the blazes am I?’ Her voice was no more than a rasp.

events.did: 雪松与桉树在这个地狱般、不比她自己卧室大的空间里散出一种不协调的宜人香气；木长凳贴着雪松板墙排列
events.verbatim: Cedar and eucalyptus created an incongruently pleasant scent in the hellish space no larger than her own bedroom. Wooden benches lined the cedar-planked walls.

events.did: 她压下那股想从腹中爬上喉咙把她掐死的恐慌
events.verbatim: She pushed down the panic that wanted to crawl from her belly up her throat to strangle her.

events.did: 每次吸气都灼伤肺叶、每次呼气都耗掉更多宝贵水分，呼吸本身就够艰难了
events.verbatim: Breathing was difficult enough when every inhalation singed her lungs and each exhalation depleted her of more precious moisture.

traps_noted.trap: L158 悬垂分词：「Holding one hand palm up and cupping the other over it, her magic built…」语法主语是 her magic，逻辑主语是 Helena（是她双掌相合）。中文若直译成『她的魔力一掌上翻、另一掌扣住』即错；正确写法是 Helena 摆出掌势、魔力在掌心积聚。
L152 悬垂分词：「Pulling moisture from the air, Helena knew her eyes were shifting…」语法上 Helena 是 knew 的主语，『抽取空气水分』是她的魔法所为；且这是认知句不是动作句，不能写成『她一边抽水一边知道』。
L170 施动者缺失：「something heavy slammed into the back of her head」是被动式、袭击者未点名。写成『Sinclair 用重物砸她后脑』是越文本断言——当时 Sinclair 在她对面说话，很可能另有同伙（U1）。
L195 虚拟语气极性：「would have been outraged at Sinclair undressing her if…didn’t…」——她实际上【没有】愤怒（干热压倒羞耻感）。误写成『她对被扒光衣服愤怒不已』把反事实当事实，极性全反。脱衣者也是『Someone』未点名。

有声/无声与极性反转：L104「‘I’m not wrong.’」带引号是【说出口】的嘴硬；L110「Oh. Dear. Goddess.」与 L113「I’m wrong.」无引号是【心声】承认自己错了。两句极性相反、一外一内，混淆会把『Hamlet 舔脸→她认输』的心理转折写丢。L92「But Cynthia would never hurt me.」同为无声心声（L95 称之为 whisper）。
L86 无 tag 说话人：「Anger rose like a swollen river. ‘Don’t scold me!…’」——『Don’t scold me』是 Helena 对 Hamlet  bark（L83）的反驳，不是别人在数落 Helena；段首叙述句极易让中文稿把说话人搞反。
L41 跨段代词：段首「He was no help.」的 He 指上一段末的 Uncle Lachlan（隔了段落），不是 Sinclair；同段「his bobbies」的 his 却指 Sinclair（他的警察）——同一段两个 his/he 指向不同的人。
L38 归属方向：「people her soft-hearted cousin had taken under her wing」——cousin＝Ellie，翅膀是 Ellie 的（her wing），被照拂的是老人；不是 Helena 收留老人。投诉对象是 Helena 的尖刻言行，投诉者是老人，提议者是 Ellie——三方不能串。
L50「She took her leave with Hamlet close on her heels.」——Hamlet 紧贴【Helena】的脚后跟她离开，方向不能写反成 Helena 跟着 Hamlet；her heels 的 her＝Helena。
L62「water stains waiting for Clio in the morning」——水渍是『等着 Clio（早上来发现）』，不是水渍沾到 Clio 身上；且 Clio 是谁本章完全没交代，中文稿不得脑补她的身份（店员？家人？）。
L62 打碎的是「three of the anti-inflammatory potions」（三瓶抗炎药剂），不是她手里那瓶 witch hazel tonic；「Fumbling」只是失手摆弄、险些脱手，原文从未说这瓶 tonic 碎了。张冠李戴会把后文 L98 她还捧着这瓶 tonic 的情节写矛盾。
Sinclair 的吞音拼写「’oping」（L125）「’eard」（L131）「’ere」（L149）是伦敦腔（h 脱落）的忠实呈现，引语必须原样保留，不得『修正』为 hoping/heard/here，也不得在中译里抹掉他的口音标记而不注。
L131「it’s akin to witchcraft」表面是恭维，实为猎巫者的威胁性试探（紧接着 Helena 嗤之以鼻、Sinclair 自夸人脉、最后摊牌『I seek a witch』）。把这句当纯赞美会漏掉整场对话的猫鼠张力；同理 L137「the quality of company I keep」暗指他与猎巫/恶势力往来。
L47 方言与习语：「as clearly as this is the nose on my face」是习语＝百分之百确定（不是字面『像鼻子一样清楚』的物象）；「canna」是苏格兰语＝cannot；「Yet.」独立成句＝『只是暂时证明不了』，三个点都易被中文稿想当然。
L50「lethal glare reminded Helena…」——Lachlan 的眼神是【提醒】她此人有军人背景，不是他真的在威胁侄女；同句「the bastard」骂的是 Sinclair 而非 Lachlan。
L116「The fox knew it.」——『狐狸』是前文既有的角色（the fox，定指），本章无任何解释；中文稿既不能当成普通动物随手带过，也不能凭空给它安身份，须存疑或按前章处理。
L122 时序：Helena 的道歉与营业时间话术是对她【以为的普通顾客】说的（她忘了锁门），说到一半认出来人才『words died in her throat』，Sinclair 到 L125 才开口。不能写成『她看见 Sinclair 后道歉打烊』——先说后认，顺序反了就丢掉她的措手不及。
L201「her core where her magic waited」——waited 看似魔力还在等她，下一句立刻揭示「was gone. In its place was nothing but mist and memory」。中文若写『魔力在核心里等待她』就把本章最大的惊悚点（魔力被抽空）写没了。
L204「‘Oh dear goddess.’ Fear, real and terrifying, filled the void…」——引号内是她【说出口】的话，引号外是叙述层对她恐惧状态的描写，不是第二句台词；两句不能合并成一段独白。
L189「salt stung her eyes」——盐的来源原文未说明（泪水？房间里的盐？），中文稿擅自补成『泪水刺痛双眼』是替文本下结论（见 U7）；应保持存疑或直译。
L59「should have filled Helena with warm joy. But instead…」——反事实结构：回家的温馨画面【本该】带来喜悦、【实际】只有空洞。写成『回家的念头让她感到温暖』极性全反。
L65「her eyes flashed silver more often than grey」——她的眼睛本色是灰、如今失控时闪银；不是『银色的眼睛多过灰色』的静态描写。同理 L152「shifting from grey to silver」是临时变色过程，两处都不能写成她有银眼睛。
L155「It could lift a ship, drown a village…」——It 回指的是前句的『泛滥的江河（水）』而非橡树；且整段是 Helena 战前给自己的壮胆联想（自由间接），不是叙述者的客观水文知识。
L71「raised a knowing brow and whined」——『knowing（了然）』是 Helena/叙述者的拟人化解读，不是 Hamlet 视角的心声；全章无 Hamlet 内心独白，中文稿不得写成『Hamlet 心里明白』式的直接心声。
